questions.q: Fill in the collective noun: A ______ of cows was grazing in the field.
questions.e: A group of cattle such as cows is called a herd.

questions.q: Write the plural of 'child'.
questions.e: 'Child' has an irregular plural, 'children'.

questions.q: Riya lost her pen, so Aman lent ______ his.
questions.e: The object form of 'she' is 'her'.

questions.q: This bag is ______; I bought it yesterday. (belonging to me)
questions.e: 'Mine' is a possessive pronoun that stands alone without a noun.

questions.q: Write the comparative form of 'tall'.
questions.e: Short adjectives form the comparative by adding '-er'.

questions.q: The tortoise walked ______. (slow)
questions.e: An adverb of manner is usually formed by adding '-ly' to the adjective.

questions.q: The sun ______ in the east. (rise)
questions.e: Universal truths are expressed in the simple present tense.

questions.q: He is ______ honest man.
questions.e: 'Honest' begins with a vowel sound (silent h), so it takes 'an'.

questions.q: There is ______ university in our town.
questions.e: 'University' begins with a 'yu' consonant sound, so it takes 'a'.

questions.q: Diwali falls ______ October this year.
questions.e: 'In' is used with months and years.

questions.q: I wanted to play outside, ______ it was raining.
questions.e: 'But' joins two ideas that contrast with each other.

questions.q: Choose the antonym of 'ancient'.
questions.e: 'Ancient' means very old; its opposite is 'modern'.

questions.q: Which punctuation mark is used at the end of a question?
questions.e: A direct question always ends with a question mark.

questions.q: Choose the synonym of 'happy'.
questions.e: 'Joyful' means feeling great happiness.

questions.q: Identify the abstract noun: 'The soldier showed great courage in the battle.'
questions.e: An abstract noun names a quality or feeling that cannot be touched, like courage.

questions.q: Write the feminine form of 'lion'.
questions.e: The feminine of 'lion' is formed by adding '-ess'.

questions.q: Identify the reflexive pronoun: 'The boy hurt himself while playing.'
questions.e: Reflexive pronouns end in '-self' or '-selves' and refer back to the subject.

questions.q: Meena is the ______ singer in our class. (good)
questions.e: 'Good' has the irregular superlative 'best'.

questions.q: Identify the adjective: 'We visited a beautiful temple in Madurai.'
questions.e: An adjective describes a noun; 'beautiful' describes the temple.

questions.q: Identify the adverb: 'The children sang sweetly at the assembly.'
questions.e: 'Sweetly' tells us how the children sang, so it is an adverb of manner.

questions.q: Yesterday, we ______ to the market. (go)
questions.e: 'Yesterday' shows past time, so the simple past 'went' is used.

questions.q: Look! The baby ______. (sleep)
questions.e: An action happening right now uses the present continuous tense.

questions.q: ______ Ganga is a holy river.
questions.e: 'The' is used before the names of rivers.

questions.q: The train leaves ______ 6 o'clock.
questions.e: 'At' is used with exact clock times.

questions.q: Rohan is fond ______ music.
questions.e: The adjective 'fond' is always followed by 'of'.

questions.q: Work hard, ______ you will fail.
questions.e: 'Or' introduces the consequence of not doing something.

questions.q: Choose the antonym of 'generous'.
questions.e: A generous person gives freely; a selfish person does not.

questions.q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
questions.e: A sentence begins with a capital letter, a comma comes before the name addressed, and a question ends with '?'.

questions.q: Which word in this sentence must begin with a capital letter? 'My uncle lives in jaipur.'
questions.e: Names of places are proper nouns and always begin with a capital letter.

questions.q:
Read: 'Anu planted a mango sapling in her garden. She watered it every morning. After three years, it gave sweet fruit.'
What did Anu plant?
questions.e: The first sentence says Anu planted a mango sapling.

questions.q: Write the plural of 'mother-in-law'.
questions.e: In compound nouns, the main word ('mother') takes the plural form.

questions.q: Between you and ______, this plan will not work.
questions.e: A preposition like 'between' takes the object pronoun 'me'.

questions.q: Arrange the adjectives in the correct order: a ______ box (wooden, old, big)
questions.e: Adjectives follow the order size, age, then material.

questions.q: Raj runs ______ than Sunil. (fast)
questions.e: 'Fast' is both adjective and adverb; its comparative is 'faster'.

questions.q: By the time we reached the station, the train ______. (leave)
questions.e: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect tense.

questions.q: She ______ in this school since 2022. (study)
questions.e: 'Since' with an action continuing to now needs the present perfect (continuous).

questions.q: He is ______ European.
questions.e: 'European' begins with a 'yu' consonant sound, so it takes 'a'.

questions.q: The thief jumped ______ the river to escape.
questions.e: 'Into' shows movement from outside to inside something.

questions.q: ______ he was ill, he went to school.
questions.e: 'Although' introduces a contrast with the main clause.

questions.q: Choose the antonym of 'expand'.
questions.e: To expand is to grow larger; to contract is to grow smaller.

questions.q: Choose the sentence in which the apostrophe is used correctly.
questions.a: The children's toys are in the box.
o: The childrens' toys are in the box.
The childrens toys are in the box.
The children's toy's are in the box.
questions.e: For a plural not ending in 's', add 's to show possession.

questions.q:
Read: 'Every winter, flocks of birds fly thousands of kilometres to the lakes of Bharatpur. They come from cold lands where the water freezes. In spring, they return home.'
The birds leave their lands because the water there ______.
questions.e: The passage says they come from cold lands where the water freezes.

questions.q:
Read the passage and answer:
Ravi's grandmother lives in a small village near Nashik. Every summer, Ravi visits her and helps her feed the cows. In the evenings, she tells him stories about her childhood. Ravi loves the village because it is quiet and green.
p: (a) Near which city is the village?
(b) Which animals does Ravi help to feed?
(c) Find a word in the passage that means 'peaceful'.
questions.e: All answers are stated directly in the passage.

questions.q:
Read the passage and answer:
The school fete was held on Saturday. Class VI set up a stall selling lemonade. They earned eight hundred rupees, which they gave to an orphanage. Their teacher was proud of them.
p: (a) On which day was the fete held?
(c) To whom did they give the money?
questions.e: All answers are stated directly in the passage.

questions.q:
Fill in each blank with the correct form of the verb in brackets:
Last Sunday, Priya (a) ______ (wake) up early. She (b) ______ (take) her dog for a walk. Now she (c) ______ (read) a book.
questions.e: Completed past actions use the simple past; an action happening now uses the present continuous.

questions.q: Read the sentence and answer: 'A swarm of bees attacked the shepherd near the river.'
p: (a) Which word is a collective noun?
questions.e: Nouns name persons, places, things or groups; 'swarm' names a group of bees.

questions.q: Read the sentence and answer: 'The tiny kitten drank warm milk.'
questions.e: Adjectives describe nouns and usually come before them.

questions.q: Each of the boys must bring ______ own lunch.
questions.e: 'Each' is singular, and 'boys' are male, so the singular pronoun 'his' is used.

questions.q: She has been ill ______ Monday.
questions.e: 'Since' is used with a point of time in the present perfect.

questions.q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence of direct speech.
questions.e: Spoken words go inside quotation marks, followed by a comma, and the reporting verb is not capitalised.

questions.q: My brother ______ cricket every evening. (play)
questions.e: A singular third-person subject takes a verb ending in '-s' in the simple present.

questions.q: The girls ______ singing in the hall.
questions.e: A plural subject takes a plural verb.

questions.q: Write the past tense of 'catch'.
questions.e: 'Catch' is an irregular verb; its past form is 'caught'.

questions.q: We ______ a film tomorrow evening. (watch)
questions.a: will watch|are watching|are going to watch|shall watch
questions.e: 'Tomorrow' shows future time.

questions.q: There isn't ______ milk left in the jug.
questions.e: 'Any' or 'much' is used with uncountable nouns in negative sentences.

questions.q: The book is ______ the shelf.
questions.e: 'On' shows something resting on a surface.

questions.q: He was tired, ______ he went to bed early.
questions.e: 'So' introduces a result.

questions.q: This is the ______ story I have ever read. (interesting)
questions.e: Long adjectives form the superlative with 'most'.

questions.q: Identify the adverb of time: 'We will leave for Shimla tomorrow.'
questions.e: 'Tomorrow' tells when the action happens.

questions.q: You ______ wear a helmet while riding a scooter. (it is the law)
questions.e: 'Must' expresses an obligation or rule.

questions.q: ______ I come in, ma'am? (asking permission)
questions.e: 'May' is used to ask for permission politely.

questions.q: Give one word for: a person who writes poems.
questions.e: A poet is someone who writes poems.

questions.q: Which punctuation mark should end this sentence? 'What a lovely garden this is'
questions.e: Exclamatory sentences end with an exclamation mark.

questions.q: Is this sentence in the active or the passive voice? 'The letter was posted by Neha.'
questions.e: The subject 'the letter' receives the action, so the sentence is passive.

questions.q: Each of the students ______ a library card.
questions.e: 'Each' is singular and takes a singular verb.

questions.q: Bread and butter ______ my favourite breakfast.
questions.e: Two nouns that form a single idea take a singular verb.

questions.q: Look! Someone ______ the window. (break)
questions.e: A recent past action with a present result uses the present perfect.

questions.q: I ______ a book when the lights went out. (read)
questions.e: An action in progress when another past action happened uses the past continuous.

questions.q: We have very ______ time left, so let's hurry.
questions.e: 'Little' is used with uncountable nouns like 'time' to mean 'hardly any'.

questions.q: She was born ______ 15th August.
questions.e: 'On' is used with dates and days.

questions.q: Divide the sweets ______ the two children.
questions.e: 'Between' is used for two people or things; 'among' for more than two.

questions.q: She will not come ______ you invite her.
questions.e: 'Unless' means 'if not'.

questions.q: He has ______ friends than his sister. (opposite of 'more')
questions.e: 'Fewer' is used with countable nouns like 'friends'.

questions.q: Please handle the glass ______. (careful)
questions.e: The adverb is formed by adding '-ly' to 'careful'.

questions.q: You ______ see a doctor about that cough. (advice)
questions.e: 'Should' is used to give advice.

questions.q:
Change into the passive voice: 'The cat chased the mouse.'
The mouse ______ by the cat.
questions.e: Simple past passive is 'was/were + past participle'.

questions.q:
Change into the passive voice: 'Ravi waters the plants.'
The plants ______ by Ravi.
questions.e: Simple present passive is 'is/are + past participle'; 'plants' is plural.

questions.q: Fill in the correct homophone: The wind ______ the leaves away. (blew/blue)
questions.e: 'Blew' is the past tense of 'blow'; 'blue' is a colour.

questions.q: The idiom 'a piece of cake' means:
questions.e: 'A piece of cake' describes something very easy to do.

questions.q:
Read: 'The lighthouse stood on a rocky island. Every night, its lamp guided ships safely past the dangerous rocks. The keeper, Mr Das, climbed 120 steps to light it.'
How many steps did Mr Das climb?
questions.a: 120|120 steps|one hundred and twenty|one hundred twenty
questions.e: The last sentence says he climbed 120 steps.

questions.q: Neither the teacher nor the students ______ present.
questions.e: With 'neither…nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'students'.

questions.q: The news ______ very good today.
questions.e: 'News' looks plural but is singular.

questions.q: They ______ for the bus for an hour when it finally arrived. (wait)
questions.e: An action continuing up to a point in the past uses the past perfect continuous.

questions.q: ______ of the two answers is correct, so you must try again.
questions.e: 'Neither' means 'not one of two'.

questions.q: The boy was accused ______ stealing.
questions.e: 'Accused' is always followed by 'of'.

questions.q: ______ had he finished his lunch than the bell rang.
questions.e: 'No sooner' is paired with 'than'.

questions.q: I ______ swim when I was five, but now I have forgotten how.
questions.e: 'Could' expresses ability in the past.

questions.q:
Change into the passive voice: 'The workers are building a bridge.'
A bridge ______ by the workers.
questions.e: Present continuous passive is 'is/are being + past participle'.

questions.q: Give one word for: a place where bees are kept.
questions.e: An apiary is a place where bees are kept; an aviary is for birds.

questions.q: Choose the correctly punctuated list sentence.
questions.a: I bought apples, bananas, mangoes and grapes.
o: I bought apples bananas, mangoes, and, grapes.
I bought, apples, bananas, mangoes and grapes.
I bought apples; bananas; mangoes and grapes
questions.e: Commas separate items in a list, and a sentence ends with a full stop.

questions.q: What kind of adverb is 'rarely' in: 'She rarely eats junk food.'?
questions.e: 'Rarely' tells how often, so it is an adverb of frequency.

questions.q: What kind of adjective is 'several' in: 'Several children were absent today.'?
questions.e: 'Several' tells how many, so it is an adjective of number.

questions.q:
Read the passage and answer:
Meera's class went on a trip to the Sundarbans. They sailed through narrow creeks lined with mangrove trees. A guide told them that the forest is home to the Royal Bengal tiger. Although they did not see a tiger, they spotted crocodiles basking on the mudbanks.
questions.e: All answers are stated directly in the passage.

questions.q:
Read the passage and answer:
Arjun had always been afraid of water. One summer, his uncle took him to a swimming pool every morning. At first, Arjun only sat on the steps. By the end of the month, he could swim across the pool without help.
p: (b) Who took him to the pool?
(c) Find a word in the passage that means 'assistance'.
questions.e: All answers are stated directly in the passage.

questions.q: Change into the passive voice by filling in the verb phrase only.
p: (a) 'Sita sings a song.' → A song ______ by Sita.
(b) 'The police caught the thief.' → The thief ______ by the police.
(c) 'Mother will bake a cake.' → A cake ______ by Mother.
questions.e: The passive uses the correct form of 'be' + past participle, matching the tense of the active.

questions.q: Fill in each blank with 'is' or 'are'.
p: (b) A number of visitors ______ waiting outside.
questions.e: 'The number' is singular, 'a number of' means 'many' (plural), and subjects like 'Mathematics' are singular.

questions.q: Fill in each blank with a suitable modal.
p: (a) It is cloudy; it ______ rain later. (possibility)
(b) Students ______ not use mobile phones in the exam hall. (prohibition)
(c) ______ you please pass the salt? (polite request)
questions.e: Modals express possibility (may), prohibition (must not) and polite requests (could).

questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.e: 'Necessary' has one 'c' and double 's'.

questions.q: He insisted ______ paying the bill.
questions.e: The verb 'insist' is followed by 'on'.

questions.q: If it rains tomorrow, we ______ at home. (stay)
questions.e: In a first conditional, the if-clause is in simple present and the main clause uses 'will'.

questions.q: Write the past participle of 'write'.
questions.e: The three forms are write, wrote, written.

questions.q: Water ______ at 100 degrees Celsius. (boil)
questions.e: Scientific facts are expressed in the simple present tense.

questions.q: One of my friends ______ from Kerala.
questions.e: The subject is 'one', which is singular.

questions.q: We ______ respect our elders. (moral duty)
questions.e: 'Should' or 'ought to' expresses moral duty.

questions.q: In 'The match was won by India', who performed the action?
questions.e: In the passive voice, the doer appears after 'by'.

questions.q:
He said, "I am tired."
He said that he ______ tired.
questions.e: When the reporting verb is in the past, present tense changes to past.

questions.q: How many clauses are there in: 'I came home and slept.'?
questions.e: There are two finite verbs, 'came' and 'slept', so there are two clauses.

questions.q: Wait here ______ I return.
questions.e: 'Until' means 'up to the time when'.

questions.q: She is good ______ mathematics.
questions.e: 'Good' is followed by 'at' when talking about skill.

questions.q: Give one word for: a person who cannot read or write.
questions.e: An illiterate person is unable to read or write.

questions.q: Fill in the correct word: The ______ of our school addressed the assembly. (principal/principle)
questions.e: 'Principal' is the head of a school; 'principle' is a rule or belief.

questions.q: Choose the synonym of 'brave'.
questions.e: 'Courageous' means brave.

questions.q: Choose the antonym of 'victory'.
questions.e: The opposite of victory is defeat.

questions.q:
Rewrite without changing the meaning: 'He is always late.'
He is ______ on time.
questions.e: 'Always late' means 'never on time'.

questions.q: The children ______ in the park since morning. (play)
questions.e: An action that began in the past and is still going on uses the present perfect continuous.

questions.q: By next June, I ______ this course. (complete)
questions.e: An action to be finished before a future time uses the future perfect.

questions.q: The committee ______ divided in its opinion.
questions.e: The pronoun 'its' shows the committee is treated as one unit, so the verb is singular.

questions.q: You ______ have told me earlier; I could have helped you.
questions.e: 'Should have' + past participle expresses regret about something not done.

questions.q:
Change into the passive voice: 'Who wrote this letter?'
By whom ______ this letter written?
questions.e: The passive of a simple past question uses 'was/were'; 'letter' is singular.

questions.q:
Change into the passive voice: 'They have finished the work.'
The work ______ by them.
questions.e: Present perfect passive is 'has/have been + past participle'.

questions.q:
She said to me, "Where do you live?"
She asked me where I ______.
questions.e: In reported questions, the word order becomes a statement and the tense moves back.

questions.q:
The teacher said, "Open your books."
The teacher ______ us to open our books.
questions.e: Commands are reported with verbs like 'told' or 'ordered' + to-infinitive.

questions.q: Identify the subordinate clause: 'The boy who won the prize is my cousin.'
questions.e: The relative clause 'who won the prize' describes 'the boy'.

questions.q: What kind of clause is in italics? 'I will call you when I reach Pune.'
questions.a: adverb clause|adverb|adverbial clause|adverb clause of time
questions.e: It tells when the action happens, so it is an adverb clause of time.

questions.q: He failed ______ he did not study.
questions.e: 'Because' introduces a reason.

questions.q: The match was postponed ______ rain.
questions.a: due to|because of|on account of|owing to
questions.e: 'Due to' or 'because of' gives the reason.

questions.q: The idiom 'to burn the midnight oil' means:
questions.a: to work late into the night
questions.e: It means to stay up late working or studying.

questions.q: Choose the synonym of 'abundant'.
questions.e: 'Abundant' means existing in large amounts, i.e. plentiful.

questions.q:
Rewrite using 'too…to': 'He is so weak that he cannot walk.'
He is ______ walk.
questions.e: 'So…that…cannot' can be changed to 'too…to'.

questions.q:
Read: 'Kavya saved coins in a clay pot for a year. On her mother's birthday, she broke the pot and bought her a silk scarf. Her mother hugged her with tears of joy.'
What did Kavya buy for her mother?
questions.e: The second sentence says she bought a silk scarf.

questions.q: I wish I ______ a bird. (be)
questions.e: Unreal wishes about the present use 'were' (subjunctive).

questions.q: Ten kilometres ______ a long distance to walk.
questions.e: A plural amount of distance treated as one quantity takes a singular verb.

questions.q: He ______ be at home; his car is in the garage. (strong deduction)
questions.e: 'Must' expresses a strong logical conclusion.

questions.q:
Change into the passive voice: 'Shut the door.'
Let the door ______.
questions.e: Imperative sentences become passive with 'Let + object + be + past participle'.

questions.q:
He said, "I will help you tomorrow."
He said that he ______ help me the next day.
questions.e: 'Will' changes to 'would' in reported speech.

questions.q:
Rita said, "What a beautiful sunset!"
Rita ______ that it was a very beautiful sunset.
questions.e: Exclamations are reported with 'exclaimed'.

questions.q:
Combine using a relative pronoun: 'I met a man. He had climbed Everest.'
I met a man ______ had climbed Everest.
questions.e: 'Who' is used as a subject relative pronoun for people.

questions.q: She is ______ a singer but also a dancer.
questions.e: 'Not only' is paired with 'but also'.

questions.q: Give one word for: a speech made without preparation.
questions.e: An extempore speech is delivered without preparation.

questions.q: Choose the antonym of 'transparent'.
questions.e: Transparent lets light through; opaque does not.

questions.q:
Rewrite as a complex sentence: 'In spite of being ill, he attended the class.'
______ he was ill, he attended the class.
questions.e: 'In spite of' becomes 'although' with a clause.

questions.q:
Change the degree: 'No other girl in the class is as tall as Anita.'
Anita is the ______ girl in the class.
questions.e: A positive degree with 'no other…as…as' becomes the superlative.

questions.q:
Read the passage and answer:
In the 1970s, villagers in the hills of Uttarakhand hugged trees to stop them from being cut down. This came to be known as the Chipko movement. 'Chipko' means 'to cling'. The women of the villages played a leading role, and their courage inspired environmental campaigns across India.
questions.e: All answers are stated directly in the passage.

questions.q:
Read the passage and answer:
Sameer's science project was a solar cooker made from a cardboard box, black paint and aluminium foil. The foil reflected sunlight into the box, while the black paint absorbed heat. On a sunny afternoon, it cooked rice in two hours. The judges awarded him the first prize.
p: (a) What reflected sunlight into the box?
(c) How long did it take to cook rice?
questions.e: All answers are stated directly in the passage.

questions.q: Change into indirect speech by filling in the blank.
p: (a) She said, "I am reading." → She said that she ______.
(b) He asked me, "Have you eaten?" → He asked me ______ I had eaten.
(c) Mother said, "Don't touch the stove." → Mother told me ______ touch the stove.
questions.e: Tenses move back, yes/no questions use 'if/whether', and negative commands use 'not to'.

questions.q: Read the sentence and answer: 'When the rain stopped, the children who had been waiting ran out to play.'
questions.e: The adverb clause tells when; the adjective clause describes 'the children'.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks to transform the sentences without changing the meaning.
p: (a) 'As soon as he saw the police, he ran away.' → No sooner had he seen the police ______ he ran away.
(b) 'He is too proud to apologise.' → He is so proud that he ______ apologise.
(c) 'She is the best dancer in the school.' → No other dancer in the school is as ______ as she.
questions.e: 'No sooner' takes 'than'; 'too…to' becomes 'so…that…cannot'; superlative becomes positive degree.

questions.q: Had you worked hard, you ______. (pass)
questions.e: A third conditional uses 'would have' + past participle in the main clause.

questions.q: The old man died ______ cholera.
questions.e: We die 'of' a disease.

questions.q: The jury ______ given its verdict.
questions.e: 'Its' shows the jury acts as one body, so the verb is singular.

questions.q: She ______ her grandparents every Diwali. (visit)
questions.e: Habitual actions use the simple present; a singular subject adds '-s'.

questions.q: Shakespeare ______ many plays. (write)
questions.e: Completed actions of a person no longer living take the simple past.

questions.q: The pair of shoes ______ under the bed.
questions.e: The subject is 'pair', which is singular.

questions.q: You ______ not bring a gift; it is optional. (absence of necessity)
questions.e: 'Need not' shows that something is not necessary.

questions.q: ______ students in the class passed; nobody failed.
questions.e: 'All' means every one of the group.

questions.q:
Change into the passive voice: 'They grow tea in Assam.'
Tea ______ in Assam.
questions.e: Simple present passive: is/are + past participle.

questions.q:
He said, "I like mangoes."
He said that he ______ mangoes.
questions.e: The simple present changes to simple past in reported speech.

questions.q: Identify the main clause: 'Although it was late, we continued working.'
questions.e: The main clause can stand alone as a complete sentence.

questions.q: He has been working here ______ ten years.
questions.e: 'For' is used with a period of time.

questions.q: Give one word for: animals that eat only plants.
questions.e: Herbivores feed only on plants.

questions.q: Fill in the correct word: Please do not ______ water. (waste/waist)
questions.e: 'Waste' means to use carelessly; 'waist' is part of the body.

questions.q: Correct the error: 'She don't like coffee.' Write the correct form of the incorrect word.
questions.e: A singular third-person subject takes 'does not'.

questions.q: One word is missing before 'best': 'She is best player in the team.' Supply it.
questions.e: Superlatives are preceded by 'the'.

questions.q:
Change to an assertive sentence: 'What a beautiful painting!'
It is a very ______ painting.
questions.e: 'What a + adjective' becomes 'very + adjective' in an assertive sentence.

questions.q: I ______ in Chennai for five years before we moved to Delhi. (live)
questions.e: An action completed before another past action uses the past perfect.

questions.q: This time tomorrow, we ______ to Singapore. (fly)
questions.e: An action in progress at a future time uses the future continuous.

questions.q: Either Raj or his friends ______ responsible for this mess.
questions.e: With 'either…or', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'friends'.

questions.q: The teacher, along with her students, ______ visiting the museum.
questions.e: Phrases like 'along with' do not change the number of the subject.

questions.q: You ______ better leave now, or you will miss the bus.
questions.e: 'Had better' is used to give strong advice.

questions.q: How ______ sugar do you need for the kheer?
questions.e: 'Much' is used with uncountable nouns like sugar.

questions.q:
Change into the passive voice: 'Somebody has stolen my bicycle.'
My bicycle ______.
questions.e: Present perfect passive: has/have been + past participle.

questions.q:
He said, "I have finished my homework."
He said that he ______ his homework.
questions.e: Present perfect changes to past perfect in reported speech.

questions.q:
She said to him, "Please help me."
She ______ him to help her.
questions.e: A request with 'please' is reported with 'requested'.

questions.q: What kind of clause is in italics? 'Tell me what you want.'
questions.e: The clause acts as the object of 'tell', so it is a noun clause.

questions.q: She congratulated me ______ my success.
questions.e: 'Congratulate' is followed by 'on'.

questions.q: The idiom 'to let the cat out of the bag' means:
questions.e: It means to reveal a secret by mistake.

questions.q: Correct the error: 'He has went to the market.' Write the correct word.
questions.e: 'Has' is followed by the past participle 'gone'.

questions.q: Correct the error: 'The furnitures in this room is new.' Write the correct form of the noun.
questions.e: 'Furniture' is uncountable and has no plural form.

questions.q:
Change to an assertive sentence: 'Who does not love his country?'
Everyone ______ his country.
questions.e: A negative rhetorical question becomes a positive assertive statement.

questions.q:
Read: 'The old banyan tree in our village square is nearly two hundred years old. Its aerial roots hang like ropes, and children swing on them. Farmers rest in its shade after work.'
What do the children swing on?
questions.e: The children swing on the aerial roots, which only look like ropes.

questions.q: Hardly ______ the station when the train left. (I / reach)
questions.e: 'Hardly' at the beginning needs inversion with the past perfect.

questions.q: Not only the students but also the principal ______ present at the function.
questions.e: With 'not only…but also', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'principal'.

questions.q: He ______ have reached Delhi by now; he left at dawn. (strong certainty)
questions.e: 'Must have' + past participle expresses a confident deduction about the past.

questions.q: She is ______ M.Sc. in Chemistry.
questions.e: 'M.Sc.' begins with the vowel sound 'em', so it takes 'an'.

questions.q:
Change into the passive voice: 'One should keep one's promises.'
Promises ______ kept.
questions.e: Modal passive: modal + be + past participle.

questions.q:
He said, "Let us go for a walk."
He ______ that they should go for a walk.
questions.e: 'Let us' expresses a suggestion and is reported with 'suggested'.

questions.q:
Combine using a relative pronoun: 'This is the pen. I lost it yesterday.'
This is the pen ______ I lost yesterday.
questions.e: 'Which' or 'that' is used for things.

questions.q: He was absent ______ school yesterday.
questions.e: 'Absent' is followed by 'from'.

questions.q: Give one word for: government by the people.
questions.e: Democracy is government by the people.

questions.q: Correct the error: 'Each of the players have received a medal.' Write the correct word.
questions.e: 'Each' is singular and takes 'has'.

questions.q:
Change into a compound sentence: 'Being tired, he went to bed.'
He was tired, ______ he went to bed.
questions.e: A participle phrase showing cause becomes a coordinate clause joined by 'so' or 'and'.

questions.q:
Remove 'too': 'The box is too heavy for me to lift.'
The box is so heavy that I ______ lift it.
questions.e: 'Too…to' becomes 'so…that…cannot'.

questions.q:
Read the passage and answer:
Every year, millions of tonnes of plastic enter the oceans. Sea turtles often mistake floating bags for jellyfish and swallow them. Scientists warn that by 2050, there may be more plastic than fish in the sea by weight. Reducing single-use plastic is the simplest way to help.
p: (a) What do sea turtles mistake floating bags for?
(b) What may outweigh fish in the sea by 2050?
(c) What is the simplest way to help?
reducing single-use plastic|reduce single-use plastic|reducing single use plastic
questions.e: All answers are stated directly in the passage.

questions.q:
Read the passage and answer:
Lakshmi runs a small library from her home in a village near Mysuru. She started it with fifty books donated by her neighbours. Today, it has over two thousand books, and children come every evening to read. Lakshmi believes that books open windows to the world.
p: (a) Near which city is Lakshmi's village?
(b) How many books did she start with?
(c) According to Lakshmi, what do books open?
questions.e: All answers are stated directly in the passage.

questions.q:
Each line has one error. Write the correct word.
(a) Last week, our school organise a tree plantation drive.
(b) Every students planted a sapling.
(c) The principal thanked all of they for their effort.
questions.e: Past time needs the past tense; 'every' takes a singular noun; a preposition takes an object pronoun.

questions.q:
In each line one word is missing. Supply the missing word.
(a) My sister fond of dancing.
(b) We went the zoo on Sunday.
(c) She has been waiting an hour.
questions.e: Each sentence needs a verb, a preposition of direction, or a preposition of duration.

questions.q: Change into the passive voice by filling in the blank.
p: (a) 'The chef is cooking dinner.' → Dinner ______ by the chef.
(b) 'Will they announce the results?' → ______ the results be announced?
(c) 'Do not tease the animals.' → The animals ______ not be teased.
questions.e: Passive forms keep the tense of the active: present continuous, future question, and prohibition.

questions.q: If I ______ about the strike, I would not have gone out. (know)
questions.e: A third conditional uses the past perfect in the if-clause.

questions.q: Choose the sentence that contains an adjective clause.
questions.a: The book that you gave me is interesting.
o: I know that you gave me a book.
When you gave me the book, I was happy.
You gave me a book and I read it.
questions.e: 'That you gave me' describes the noun 'book', so it is an adjective clause.

questions.q: You ______ not have bought milk; there was plenty in the fridge. (it was unnecessary)
questions.e: 'Need not have' + past participle means something was done but was unnecessary.

questions.q: The Earth ______ around the Sun. (revolve)
questions.e: Universal truths take the simple present tense.

questions.q: We ______ him at the airport last night. (meet)
questions.e: 'Last night' shows completed past time, so the simple past is used.

questions.q: Everyone in the family ______ to watch cricket.
questions.e: 'Everyone' is singular and takes a singular verb.

questions.q: ______ we go for a walk? (suggestion)
questions.e: 'Shall we…?' is used to make a suggestion.

questions.q: ______ sun sets in the west.
questions.e: 'The' is used before unique objects like the sun.

questions.q:
Change into the passive voice: 'She opened the gate.'
The gate ______ by her.
questions.e: Simple past passive: was/were + past participle.

questions.q:
"I can swim," said Tara.
Tara said that she ______ swim.
questions.e: 'Can' changes to 'could' in reported speech.

questions.q: Identify the subordinating conjunction: 'I stayed indoors because it was snowing.'
questions.e: 'Because' introduces the subordinate clause of reason.

questions.q: She is afraid ______ the dark.
questions.e: 'Afraid' is followed by 'of'.

questions.q: Give one word for: a person who does not eat meat.
questions.e: A vegetarian does not eat meat.

questions.q: Fill in the correct word: I could not ______ the noise. (bare/bear)
questions.e: 'Bear' means to tolerate; 'bare' means uncovered.

questions.q: Which word must be removed to correct: 'She is more taller than her brother.'?
questions.e: 'Taller' is already comparative, so 'more' is not needed.

questions.q: Correct the error: 'He go to school by bus every day.' Write the correct word.
questions.e: A singular subject in the simple present takes 'goes'.

questions.q:
Change to a negative sentence: 'Only Ravi can solve this.'
______ but Ravi can solve this.
questions.e: 'Only' in an affirmative becomes 'none but' in a negative sentence.

questions.q: When I reached the hall, the programme ______. (already begin)
questions.e: The earlier of two past actions uses the past perfect.

questions.q: According to the timetable, our exams ______ next Monday. (start)
questions.e: Timetabled future events often use the simple present.

questions.q: Fifty rupees ______ too much for this pen.
questions.e: A sum of money treated as one amount takes a singular verb.

questions.q: The Prime Minister and the President ______ arrived at the venue.
questions.e: Two different persons joined by 'and' take a plural verb.

questions.q: You ______ not smoke here; it is a hospital. (prohibition)
questions.e: 'Must not' expresses prohibition.

questions.q: It was ______ unique experience.
questions.e: 'Unique' begins with a 'yu' consonant sound, so it takes 'a'.

questions.q:
Change into the passive voice: 'Did she invite you?'
______ you invited by her?
questions.e: The passive of a simple past question uses 'was/were'; 'you' takes 'were'.

questions.q:
Change into the passive voice: 'People speak English all over the world.'
English ______ all over the world.
questions.e: Simple present passive: is/are + past participle.

questions.q:
He said, "I was busy yesterday."
He said that he ______ busy the previous day.
questions.e: Simple past changes to past perfect in reported speech.

questions.q:
The boy said, "Hurrah! We have won the match."
The boy exclaimed with ______ that they had won the match.
questions.e: 'Hurrah' expresses joy.

questions.q: What kind of clause is in italics? 'The place where we camped was beautiful.'
questions.e: The clause describes the noun 'place', so it is an adjective clause.

questions.q: He was ______ his wits' end.
questions.e: The fixed phrase is 'at one's wits' end'.

questions.q: The idiom 'to turn over a new leaf' means:
questions.a: to change one's behaviour for the better
questions.e: It means to start behaving in a better way.

questions.q: Correct the error: 'I am knowing the answer now.' Write the correct verb.
questions.e: Stative verbs like 'know' are not used in the continuous form.

questions.q:
Rewrite using 'unless': 'If you do not hurry, you will miss the bus.'
Unless you ______, you will miss the bus.
questions.e: 'Unless' already means 'if not', so the verb is positive.

questions.q:
Read: 'The monsoon reached Kerala two days early this year. Farmers welcomed the rain and began sowing paddy. However, heavy showers flooded some low-lying fields.'
What did the farmers begin sowing?
questions.e: The second sentence says they began sowing paddy.

questions.q: It is high time we ______. (leave)
questions.e: 'It is high time' is followed by the simple past.

questions.q: A large number of people ______ gathered outside the stadium.
questions.e: 'A number of' means 'many' and takes a plural verb.

questions.q: He ______ to swim when he was young, but he has forgotten how.
questions.e: 'Used to' expresses a past habit that no longer exists.

questions.q: There were ______ errors in his essay that the teacher returned it.
questions.e: 'So many' is used with countable nouns before a 'that' clause of result.

questions.q:
Change into the passive voice: 'They say that he is honest.'
He ______ to be honest.
questions.e: 'They say that…' becomes '…is said to…' in the passive.

questions.q:
She said to me, "Will you come to my party?"
She asked me ______ I would come to her party.
questions.e: Yes/no questions are reported with 'if' or 'whether'.

questions.q: Identify the noun clause: 'What he said surprised everyone.'
questions.e: 'What he said' is the subject of the verb 'surprised', so it is a noun clause.

questions.q: She has been suffering ______ fever for three days.
questions.e: 'Suffer' is followed by 'from'.

questions.q: Give one word for: a person who remains calm and unaffected by pleasure or pain.
questions.e: A stoic endures pleasure and pain without showing feelings.

questions.q: Correct the error: 'Neither of the answers are correct.' Write the correct word.
questions.e: 'Neither' is singular and takes 'is'.

questions.q:
Change into a complex sentence: 'He confessed his guilt.'
He confessed ______ he was guilty.
questions.e: A noun clause introduced by 'that' replaces the noun phrase.

questions.q:
Change the degree: 'Very few cities in India are as big as Mumbai.'
Mumbai is ______ than most other cities in India.
questions.e: 'Very few…as…as' becomes the comparative with 'than most other'.

questions.q:
Read the passage and answer:
At four in the morning, the fishing boats of Kovalam set out to sea. The fishermen use the stars to find their way and return by noon with their catch. Their wives sell the fish at the local market, bargaining loudly with customers. In recent years, rising sea temperatures have reduced the catch, worrying the community.
p: (a) At what time do the boats set out?
four in the morning|at four in the morning|4 in the morning|4 am|4 a.m.
(b) What do the fishermen use to find their way?
(c) What has reduced the catch in recent years?
questions.e: All answers are stated directly in the passage.

questions.q:
Read the passage and answer:
Nandini had practised the veena for six years before her first public concert. On the evening of the performance, her hands trembled as she tuned the strings. But once she began the first raga, her fear melted away. The audience rose to give her a standing ovation.
p: (a) For how many years had Nandini practised?
(b) What trembled as she tuned the strings?
(c) What melted away once she began?
questions.e: All answers are stated directly in the passage.

questions.q:
Each line has one error. Write the correct word.
(a) The students was waiting for the results.
(b) Mumbai is one of the busiest city in the world.
(c) He has been living here since five years.
questions.e: A plural subject takes 'were'; 'one of the' takes a plural noun; a period of time takes 'for'.

questions.q:
In each line one word is missing. Supply the missing word.
(a) Neither Rahul nor Sameer present yesterday.
(b) She insisted going alone.
(c) I have living in Pune for a decade.
questions.e: A verb, a preposition after 'insisted', and 'been' for the present perfect continuous are missing.

questions.q: Rewrite each sentence as directed by filling in the missing word, keeping the meaning the same.
p: (a) 'He is so poor that he cannot buy a car.' → He is too poor ______ buy a car.
(b) 'She works hard to succeed.' → She works hard so ______ she may succeed.
(c) 'He was not only intelligent but also hardworking.' → He was ______ intelligent and hardworking.
questions.e: 'So…that…cannot' becomes 'too…to'; purpose uses 'so that'; 'not only…but also' can become 'both…and'.

questions.q:
The teacher said, "The Earth is round."
The teacher said that the Earth ______ round.
questions.e: Universal truths do not change tense in reported speech.

questions.q:
Change into the passive voice: 'Let him do the work.'
Let the work ______ by him.
questions.e: 'Let' passive: Let + object + be + past participle.

questions.q: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
questions.a: I have been waiting for two hours.
o: I am waiting since two hours.
I have been waiting since two hours.
I was waiting since two hours.
questions.e: A period of time takes 'for' with the present perfect continuous.

questions.q: Two little hands go clap, clap, ______.
questions.e: In the poem the hands go clap, clap, clap.

questions.q: In the morning we say, 'Good ______!'
questions.e: We greet people with 'Good morning' in the morning.

questions.q: Which letter comes after A?
questions.e: The alphabet begins A, B, C.

questions.q: The opposite of big is ______.
questions.e: Big and small are opposites.

questions.q: Which word rhymes with cat: cow, bat, cup?
questions.e: Cat and bat end with the same sound -at.

questions.q: One pen, many ______.
questions.e: We add s to make many: pen, pens.

questions.q: Find the naming word: run, ball, jump.
questions.e: Ball is the name of a thing, so it is a naming word.

questions.q: Find the action word: book, eat, tree.
questions.e: Eat tells us what we do, so it is an action word.

questions.q: We say 'an' before ______: apple or ball?
questions.e: Apple begins with the vowel sound a, so we say an apple.

questions.q: A cow says ______.
questions.e: A cow says moo.

questions.q: Two little legs go tap, tap, ______.
questions.e: In the poem the legs go tap, tap, tap.

questions.q: When someone gives you a gift, you say '______ you'.
questions.e: We say 'Thank you' when someone gives us something.

questions.q: How many letters are there in the English alphabet?
questions.e: The English alphabet has 26 letters, from A to Z.

questions.q: The opposite of hot is ______.
questions.e: Hot and cold are opposites.

questions.q: Two little eyes are open ______.
questions.e: The poem says: Two little eyes are open wide.

questions.q: One little head goes side to ______.
questions.e: The poem says: One little head goes side to side.

questions.q: At night, before sleeping, we say 'Good ______'.
questions.e: We say 'Good night' before going to sleep.

questions.q: Which letter comes between C and E?
questions.e: The order is C, D, E.

questions.q: A, E, I, O and U are called ______.
questions.e: A, E, I, O, U are the five vowels.

questions.q: Which word rhymes with sun: bun, cup, sit?
questions.e: Sun and bun end with the same sound -un.

questions.q: Fill in a word that rhymes with cat: The cat sat on a ______.
questions.e: Cat, sat and mat all end with -at.

questions.q: One box, many ______.
questions.e: Words ending in x take es: box, boxes.

questions.q: Meera has a doll. Which word is the name of a toy?
questions.e: Doll is the name of a toy.

questions.q: Birds ______ in the sky.
questions.e: Fly is the action birds do in the sky.

questions.q: Which word takes 'a' before it: owl, egg, kite?
questions.e: Kite begins with the sound k, so we say a kite.

questions.q: A baby cat is called a ______.
questions.e: The young one of a cat is a kitten.

questions.q: A duck says ______.
questions.e: A duck says quack, quack.

questions.q: The opposite of up is ______.
questions.e: Up and down are opposites.

questions.q: When you make a mistake, you say ______.
questions.e: We say 'Sorry' when we make a mistake.

questions.q: We ______ with our eyes.
questions.e: We see with our eyes.

questions.q: One child, many ______.
questions.e: Child does not take s. Many child are children.

questions.q: Arjun is tall. His little sister is ______.
questions.e: Tall and short are opposites.

questions.q: Which word does NOT rhyme: hen, pen, cup, ten?
questions.e: Hen, pen and ten end with -en, but cup does not.

questions.q: Which letter comes just before M?
questions.e: The order is K, L, M, N.

questions.q: Riya goes to school. Which naming word is a place?
questions.e: School is the name of a place.

questions.q: Arjun kicks the ball. Which word tells what Arjun does?
questions.e: Kicks is the action word.

questions.q: We say 'an' before ______: umbrella or kite?
questions.e: Umbrella begins with the vowel sound u, so we say an umbrella.

questions.q: A dog lives in a ______.
questions.e: A dog's house is a kennel. A horse lives in a stable.

questions.q: You want a pencil from your friend. Which magic word will you use?
questions.e: We say 'please' when we ask for something.

questions.q: In the poem 'Two Little Hands', how many little heads are there?
questions.e: The poem says: One little head goes side to side.

questions.q: One leaf, many ______.
questions.e: Leaf changes f to v and adds es: leaves.

questions.q: The opposite of day is ______.
questions.e: Day and night are opposites.

questions.q: Read: Two little hands go clap, clap, clap. Two little legs go tap, tap, tap.
questions.e: The hands clap and the legs tap. We have two hands.

questions.q: Pick the rhyming word.
p: (a) Which word rhymes with ball: tall or big?
(b) Which word rhymes with king: ring or rope?
(c) Which word rhymes with red: bed or cup?
questions.e: Rhyming words end with the same sound: ball-tall, king-ring, red-bed.

questions.q: Write the word for many.
questions.e: Cup adds s, bus adds es, and man changes to men.

questions.q: Answer about animals.
p: (a) A baby dog is called a ______.
(b) A baby cow is called a ______.
(c) What sound does a dog make?
questions.e: A puppy is a baby dog and a calf is a baby cow. A dog says bow-wow.

questions.q: Read: Riya eats a mango.
p: (a) Which naming word is a fruit?
(c) What is the name of the girl?
questions.e: Riya and mango are naming words. Eats is the action word.

questions.q: Which of these takes 'an' before it: ink, pen, cup?
questions.e: Ink begins with the vowel sound i, so we say an ink pot or an ink.

questions.q: Riya's glass is full. Arjun's glass has no water. Arjun's glass is ______.
questions.e: Full and empty are opposites.

questions.q: When you leave your friend's house, you say ______.
questions.e: We say 'Goodbye' when we leave.

questions.q: Little drops of ______, little grains of sand.
questions.e: The poem begins: Little drops of water, little grains of sand.

questions.t: Story: The Monkey and the Crocodile
questions.q: In 'The Smart Monkey', the monkey's friend is a ______.
questions.e: The monkey makes friends with a crocodile who lives in the river.

questions.q: The opposite of fast is ______.
questions.e: Fast and slow are opposites.

questions.q: Which word rhymes with star: car, sun, sky?
questions.e: Star and car end with the same sound -ar.

questions.q: One book, two ______.
questions.e: We add s to book to make books.

questions.q: Find the naming word: Delhi, go, red.
questions.e: Delhi is the name of a place, so it is a naming word.

questions.q: Fish ______ in water.
questions.e: Swim is what fish do in water.

questions.q: The grass is ______ in colour.
questions.e: Green describes the colour of grass.

questions.q: How many days are there in a week?
questions.e: A week has seven days, from Sunday to Saturday.

questions.q: Riya is my friend. ______ is kind.
questions.e: We use she for a girl.

questions.q: The opposite of happy is ______.
questions.e: Happy and sad are opposites.

questions.q: One cow, many ______.
questions.e: We add s to cow to make cows.

questions.q: Which day comes after Monday?
questions.e: The order is Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday.

questions.t: Story: The Monkey and the Crocodile
questions.q: In 'The Smart Monkey', where did the crocodile live?
questions.a: river|in the river|in a river|water|in water
questions.e: The crocodile lived in the river near the monkey's tree.

questions.q: Little drops of water, little grains of sand, make the mighty ______.
questions.e: Many little drops of water together make the mighty ocean.

questions.q: Little grains of sand make the pleasant ______.
questions.e: The poem says the little grains of sand make the pleasant land.

questions.t: Story: The Monkey and the Crocodile
questions.q: The crocodile's wife wanted to eat the monkey's ______.
questions.e: The crocodile's wife wanted the monkey's heart, so the crocodile tricked the monkey.

questions.q: The opposite of open is ______.
questions.e: Open and close are opposites.

questions.q: Which word rhymes with rain: train, rail, road?
questions.e: Rain and train end with the same sound -ain.

questions.q: One bench, many ______.
questions.e: Words ending in ch take es: bench, benches.

questions.q: One baby, many ______.
questions.e: Baby changes y to i and adds es: babies.

questions.q: Find the naming word: The bird sings.
questions.e: Bird is the name of an animal, so it is a naming word.

questions.q: Find the action word: Meera writes a letter.
questions.e: Writes tells what Meera does.

questions.q: Find the describing word: Arjun has a red kite.
questions.e: Red tells us about the kite, so it is a describing word.

questions.q: An elephant is very ______. (big or small)
questions.e: Big describes the size of an elephant.

questions.q: Which is the first month of the year?
questions.e: The year begins with January.

questions.q: Arjun and Meera are playing. ______ are happy.
questions.e: We use they for more than one person.

questions.q: This is a pen. ______ is blue.
questions.e: We use it for a thing.

questions.q: A dog ______ at strangers.
questions.e: Barks is the action a dog does.

questions.q: The opposite of come is ______.
questions.e: Come and go are opposites.

questions.t: Story: The Monkey and the Crocodile
questions.q: To save himself, the monkey said he had left his heart on the ______.
questions.e: The clever monkey said his heart was on the tree, so the crocodile took him back.

questions.t: Story: The Monkey and the Crocodile
questions.q: The monkey saved himself by using his ______.
questions.e: The monkey thought quickly and used his brain to escape.

questions.q: Which word does NOT rhyme: fan, man, can, cap?
questions.e: Fan, man and can end with -an, but cap does not.

questions.q: One tooth, many ______.
questions.e: Tooth changes to teeth for many.

questions.q: We light lamps on Diwali. Which naming word is a festival?
questions.e: Diwali is the name of a festival.

questions.q: Yesterday Riya ______ with a ball. (play or played)
questions.e: Yesterday tells us it is past, so we use played.

questions.q: Sugar tastes ______.
questions.e: Sweet describes the taste of sugar.

questions.q: Today is Friday. Tomorrow will be ______.
questions.e: Saturday comes after Friday.

questions.q: Which month comes just before May?
questions.e: The order is March, April, May.

questions.q: Give ______ the book. (I or me)
questions.e: We say 'Give me the book', not 'Give I the book'.

questions.q: The opposite of early is ______.
questions.e: Early and late are opposites.

questions.q: In the poem, the drops of water and grains of sand are very ______.
questions.e: The poem shows that little things together make big things.

questions.q: Read: Little drops of water, little grains of sand, make the mighty ocean and the pleasant land.
p: (b) What do the little drops of water make?
questions.e: Sand and land rhyme. Little drops of water together make the big ocean.

questions.t: Story: The Monkey and the Crocodile
questions.q: Think about the story 'The Smart Monkey'.
p: (a) Who carried the monkey on his back?
(b) Who was smart in the story?
(c) Was the crocodile a true friend? Write yes or no.
questions.e: The crocodile carried the monkey to trick him, but the smart monkey escaped. A true friend does not trick you.

questions.q: Write the word for many.
questions.e: Bus takes es; man becomes men and mouse becomes mice.

questions.q: Use he, she, it or they in place of the words.
questions.e: He is for a boy, it is for an animal or thing, and they is for more than one.

questions.q: Read: Meera sees a big yellow bus.
p: (a) Which word tells the size of the bus?
(b) Which word tells the colour of the bus?
questions.e: Big and yellow describe the bus. Sees is the action word.

questions.q: Independence Day is on 15th ______.
questions.e: India celebrates Independence Day on 15th August.

questions.q: Fill in a word that rhymes with goat: I see a goat in a ______.
questions.e: Goat and boat end with the same sound -oat.

questions.q: Which word is NOT an action word: jump, sing, chair, read?
questions.e: Chair is a naming word. Jump, sing and read are action words.

questions.q: Who wrote the poem 'Paper Boats'?
questions.e: 'Paper Boats' is a poem by Rabindranath Tagore.

questions.q: Find the noun: The peacock dances.
questions.e: Peacock is the name of a bird, so it is a noun.

questions.q: Meera is reading. ______ is reading a story.
questions.e: She is the pronoun used in place of a girl's name.

questions.q: Find the verb: Birds build nests.
questions.e: Build is the action word, so it is the verb.

questions.q: Find the adjective: Riya has a sweet voice.
questions.e: Sweet describes the voice, so it is an adjective.

questions.q: Write the plural of 'flower'.
questions.e: We add s to flower to make flowers.

questions.q: The opposite of heavy is ______.
questions.e: Heavy and light are opposites.

questions.q: Which mark comes at the end of a question?
questions.e: A question ends with a question mark (?).

questions.q: Which word rhymes with boat: goat, boot, bat?
questions.e: Boat and goat end with the same sound -oat.

questions.q: Which word takes 'an' before it: elephant, tiger, lion?
questions.e: Elephant begins with a vowel sound, so we say an elephant.

questions.q: A noun is a ______ word.
questions.e: A noun names a person, place, animal or thing.

questions.q: Verbs are ______ words.
questions.e: A verb tells us what someone or something does.

questions.q: The opposite of clean is ______.
questions.e: Clean and dirty are opposites.

questions.q: In 'Paper Boats', the child floats his boats down the running ______.
questions.e: The poem begins: Day by day I float my paper boats one by one down the running stream.

questions.q: With which flowers does the child load his paper boats?
questions.e: He loads his little boats with shiuli flowers from his garden.

questions.q: In what kind of letters does the child write his name on the boats?
questions.e: He writes his name in big black letters.

questions.q: Riya and I are friends. ______ go to school together.
questions.e: Riya and I together can be replaced by we.

questions.q: Give the ball to Arjun. Give the ball to ______.
questions.e: After 'to' we use him, not he.

questions.q: Riya ______ a song every day. (sing or sings)
questions.e: With one person (Riya) in the present tense, the verb takes s: sings.

questions.q: Find the adjective: Arjun ate a juicy mango.
questions.e: Juicy describes the mango.

questions.q: Write the plural of 'glass'.
questions.e: Words ending in ss take es: glass, glasses.

questions.q: Write the plural of 'story'.
questions.e: When a word ends in consonant + y, change y to i and add es: stories.

questions.q: The opposite of remember is ______.
questions.e: Remember and forget are opposites.

questions.q: Every sentence begins with a ______ letter.
questions.e: The first word of a sentence always begins with a capital letter.

questions.q: Which mark is used at the end of a telling sentence?
questions.e: A telling sentence ends with a full stop (.).

questions.q: Which word takes 'a' before it: orange, umbrella, mango?
questions.e: Mango begins with a consonant sound, so we say a mango.

questions.q: Which word rhymes with bright: night or day?
questions.e: Bright and night end with the same sound -ight.

questions.q: We went to the zoo. Which noun names a place?
questions.e: Zoo is the name of a place.

questions.q: Write the past tense of 'jump'.
questions.e: We add ed to jump to make the past tense jumped.

questions.q: The opposite of inside is ______.
questions.e: Inside and outside are opposites.

questions.q: Which word takes 'an' before it: hour, horse, house?
questions.e: In hour the h is silent, so it begins with a vowel sound: an hour.

questions.q: This bag belongs to me. It is ______.
questions.e: Mine shows that something belongs to me.

questions.q: Write the past tense of 'go'.
questions.e: Go is an irregular verb; its past tense is went.

questions.q: Write the past tense of 'eat'.
questions.e: Eat is an irregular verb; its past tense is ate.

questions.q: Arjun is tall. Riya is ______ than Arjun.
questions.e: When we compare two people we add er: taller.

questions.q: Write the plural of 'knife'.
questions.e: Knife changes fe to v and adds es: knives.

questions.q: The opposite of kind is ______.
questions.e: Adding un to kind makes its opposite, unkind.

questions.q: Which word must begin with a capital letter: city, delhi, river?
questions.e: Delhi is the name of a particular place, so it begins with a capital letter.

questions.q: Which word does NOT rhyme: cake, lake, make, cook?
questions.e: Cake, lake and make end with -ake, but cook does not.

questions.q: Find the noun: The children were very happy.
questions.e: Children names people, so it is a noun.

questions.q: The child hopes that the shiuli flowers, 'these blooms of the ______', will reach land safely.
questions.e: Shiuli flowers bloom at night and fall at dawn, so the poet calls them blooms of the dawn.

questions.q: Which word takes 'an' before it: university, umbrella, uniform?
questions.e: Umbrella begins with the vowel sound 'uh'. University, uniform and unicorn begin with a 'yoo' sound, so they take a.

questions.q: Read: 'In big black letters I write my name on them and the name of the village where I live.'
p: (a) What does the child write on the boats first?
(b) What else does he write on them?
name of the village|village name|the name of the village|village|name of his village
(c) Write one describing word used for 'letters'.
questions.e: The child writes his own name and the name of his village in big black letters, hoping someone far away will read them.

questions.q: Write the plural.
questions.e: Foot becomes feet, woman becomes women and leaf becomes leaves.

questions.q: Write the past tense of each verb.
questions.e: Walk adds ed, but write and see are irregular: wrote and saw.

questions.q: Correct this sentence: where is arjun
p: (a) Which first word needs a capital letter?
(b) Which name needs a capital letter?
(c) Which mark should come at the end?
questions.e: The correct sentence is: Where is Arjun?

questions.q: Read: Riya has a parrot. Riya feeds the parrot daily.
questions.e: She feeds it daily. It is her parrot.

questions.q: Good, better, ______.
questions.e: Good is irregular: good, better, best.

questions.q: The opposite of brave is ______.
questions.e: A brave person is not afraid; the opposite is cowardly or timid.

questions.q: How many nouns are there in: 'Arjun put the book on the table.'?
questions.e: Arjun, book and table are the three nouns.

questions.t: Poem: One Thing at a Time
questions.q: Work while you work, ______ while you play.
questions.e: The poem begins: Work while you work, play while you play.

questions.q: Braille is a script used by people who cannot ______.
questions.e: Braille helps blind or visually impaired people read and write by touch.

questions.q: Find the proper noun: Arjun lives in a village.
questions.e: Arjun is the name of a particular person, so it is a proper noun.

questions.q: Write the past tense of 'sing'.
questions.e: Sing, sang, sung. The simple past is sang.

questions.q: Find the adjective: The old man sat on a bench.
questions.e: Old describes the man, so it is an adjective.

questions.q: Find the adverb: The tortoise walks slowly.
questions.e: Slowly tells how the tortoise walks, so it is an adverb.

questions.q: The book is ______ the table. (It is lying on top of it.)
questions.e: On shows that something is resting on top of something else.

questions.q: Riya ______ Meera are sisters.
questions.e: And joins two names together.

questions.q: The antonym (opposite) of strong is ______.
questions.e: Strong and weak are antonyms.

questions.q: Which mark shows surprise or strong feeling?
questions.e: The exclamation mark (!) shows strong feeling, as in 'What a lovely day!'

questions.q: Who invented the Braille script?
questions.e: The script is named after its inventor, Louis Braille.

questions.q: Find the common noun: Meera has a parrot.
questions.e: Parrot is a general name for a kind of bird, so it is a common noun.

questions.q: Write a synonym of 'big'.
questions.e: Large and huge mean the same as big.

questions.t: Poem: One Thing at a Time
questions.q: This is the way to be happy and ______.
questions.e: The poem says: This is the way to be happy and gay. Here gay means cheerful.

questions.t: Poem: One Thing at a Time
questions.q: All that you do, do with your ______.
questions.e: Might means full strength; we should do every task with full effort.

questions.t: Poem: One Thing at a Time
questions.q: Things done by ______ are never done right.
questions.e: Work done halfway or carelessly is never done well.

questions.q: Braille letters are made of raised ______.
questions.e: Each Braille letter is a pattern of raised dots felt with the fingertips.

questions.q: How many dot positions are there in one Braille cell?
questions.e: A Braille cell has six dot positions, in two columns of three.

questions.q: Fill in the collective noun: a ______ of cows.
questions.e: A group of cows is called a herd.

questions.q: Look! The children ______ playing. (is or are)
questions.e: Children is plural, so we use are.

questions.q: Riya ______ a letter yesterday. (write)
questions.e: Yesterday shows the past, so write becomes wrote.

questions.q: Write the comparative of 'big'.
questions.e: Big doubles the g before er: bigger.

questions.q: The rabbit ran ______. (quick or quickly)
questions.e: Quickly is an adverb that tells how the rabbit ran.

questions.q: We go to school ______ bus.
questions.e: We use by for means of travel: by bus, by train.

questions.q: I wanted to play, ______ it was raining.
questions.e: But joins two ideas that are in contrast.

questions.q: Write a synonym of 'happy'.
questions.e: Glad, joyful and cheerful mean the same as happy.

questions.q: Which mark separates the items in a list, as in: apples, mangoes, bananas?
questions.e: Commas separate items in a list.

questions.q: Write the feminine of 'king'.
questions.e: King is masculine; queen is feminine.

questions.q: The bird flew ______ the window into the room.
questions.e: Through means from one side to the other of an opening.

questions.q: Write the antonym of 'ancient'.
questions.e: Ancient means very old; its opposite is modern.

questions.t: Poem: One Thing at a Time
questions.q: According to the poem 'One Thing at a Time', what is a very good rule?
questions.a: one thing at a time|one thing each time
questions.e: The poem says: One thing each time, and that done well, is a very good rule.

questions.t: Poem: One Thing at a Time
questions.q: Moments are useless, ______ away.
questions.e: Trifled away means wasted on unimportant things; such moments are useless.

questions.q: Louis Braille was born in which country?
questions.e: Louis Braille was born in 1809 in Coupvray, France.

questions.q: World Braille Day is celebrated on 4th ______.
questions.e: World Braille Day is on 4 January, the birthday of Louis Braille.

questions.q: Tomorrow Arjun ______ his grandmother. (visit)
questions.e: Tomorrow shows the future, so we use will visit.

questions.q: Write the superlative of 'bad'.
questions.e: Bad is irregular: bad, worse, worst.

questions.q: Which word is an adverb of time: yesterday, slowly, here?
questions.e: Yesterday tells when; slowly tells how and here tells where.

questions.q: Riya went to bed early ______ she was tired.
questions.e: Because gives the reason for an action.

questions.q: Arjun was born ______ 2015.
questions.e: We use in with years and months, on with days and dates.

questions.q: Which mark is used in the word 'don't'?
questions.e: The apostrophe shows that a letter is left out: do not becomes don't.

questions.q: Write a synonym of 'begin'.
questions.e: Begin and start mean the same.

questions.q: Fill in the collective noun: a ______ of birds.
questions.e: A group of birds is called a flock.

questions.t: Poem: One Thing at a Time
questions.q: Read: 'One thing each time, and that done well, is a very good rule, as many can tell.'
p: (c) How many things should we do at a time?
questions.e: Well and tell rhyme. The poet advises doing one thing at a time and doing it well.

questions.q: About Louis Braille:
p: (a) At what age did Louis Braille lose his sight?
(b) In which year was Louis Braille born?
(c) With which part of the hand do people read Braille?
questions.e: Louis Braille, born in 1809, lost his sight at the age of three after an accident; Braille is read by touching the dots with the fingertips.

questions.q: Read: Meera eats an apple.
p: (b) Future tense: Meera ______ an apple tomorrow.
(c) Present continuous: Meera ______ an apple now.
questions.e: Eat becomes ate in the past, will eat in the future and is eating in the present continuous.

questions.q: Write the correct degree of the adjective.
questions.e: Happy becomes happier, beautiful becomes most beautiful and far becomes farther or further.

questions.q: Fill in the correct preposition.
questions.e: Between is used for two, from or off shows movement away, and under shows below something.

questions.q: Would you like tea ______ milk?
questions.e: Or is used to give a choice.

questions.q: Find the adverb: Arjun always finishes his homework on time.
questions.e: Always tells how often Arjun finishes his homework, so it is an adverb of frequency.

questions.q: How many capital letters are needed in: 'meera lives in pune.'?
questions.e: Meera begins the sentence and is a name; Pune is a place name: Meera lives in Pune.

questions.q: Who wrote the poem 'The Rainbow' that begins 'Boats sail on the rivers'?
questions.e: 'The Rainbow' is a poem by Christina Rossetti.

questions.q: Boats sail on the rivers, and ships sail on the ______.
questions.e: The poem begins: Boats sail on the rivers, and ships sail on the seas.

questions.q: Find the proper noun: The Ganga is a holy river.
questions.e: Ganga is the name of a particular river, so it is a proper noun.

questions.q: Arjun said, '______ am hungry.'
questions.e: I is the pronoun used as the subject with am.

questions.q: Write the past tense of 'bring'.
questions.e: Bring is irregular: bring, brought, brought.

questions.q: Find the adjective: Riya wore a beautiful dress.
questions.e: Beautiful describes the dress.

questions.q: Find the adverb: The baby slept peacefully.
questions.e: Peacefully tells how the baby slept.

questions.q: The cat jumped ______ the wall. (over or of)
questions.e: Over shows movement above and across something.

questions.q: Arjun is poor ______ honest.
questions.e: But joins two contrasting ideas.

questions.q: Write the antonym of 'arrive'.
questions.e: Arrive means to reach; depart means to leave.

questions.q: A sentence that asks something ends with a ______.
questions.e: An interrogative sentence ends with a question mark.

questions.q: Fill in the collective noun: a ______ of bees.
questions.e: A group of bees is called a swarm.

questions.q: Write a synonym of 'small'.
questions.e: Little and tiny mean the same as small.

questions.q: Riya ______ football every Sunday. (play)
questions.e: Habits are shown by the simple present; with Riya the verb takes s: plays.

questions.q: In 'The Rainbow', what sails across the sky?
questions.e: The poet says clouds that sail across the sky are prettier far than boats and ships.

questions.q: 'The bow that bridges heaven' in the poem means the ______.
questions.e: The arch-shaped rainbow is called a bow that bridges heaven.

questions.q: The rainbow builds a road from earth to ______.
questions.e: The poem says the rainbow builds a road from earth to sky.

questions.q: Write the feminine of 'nephew'.
questions.e: Nephew is masculine; niece is feminine.

questions.q: Riya and Meera won the prize. The prize is ______.
questions.e: Theirs is a possessive pronoun that stands alone.

questions.q: Arjun hurt ______ while playing.
questions.e: Himself is the reflexive pronoun for he.

questions.q: Look! It ______. (rain)
questions.e: 'Look!' shows an action happening now, so we use the present continuous: is raining.

questions.q: Write the comparative of 'beautiful'.
questions.e: Long adjectives use more for the comparative: more beautiful.

questions.q: Find the adverb of place: Please sit here.
questions.e: Here tells where to sit, so it is an adverb of place.

questions.q: The meeting is ______ Monday.
questions.e: We use on with days and dates.

questions.q: Hurry up, ______ you will miss the bus.
questions.e: Or here means 'if not'; it warns of what will happen.

questions.q: Write the homophone of 'see' (a large body of salt water).
questions.e: See and sea sound the same but have different spellings and meanings.

questions.q: 'Shut the door.' What kind of sentence is this?
questions.e: A sentence that gives a command or order is an imperative sentence.

questions.q: Write the plural of 'potato'.
questions.e: Potato adds es: potatoes.

questions.q: Find the adjective of number: Riya bought five pencils.
questions.e: Five tells how many pencils, so it is an adjective of number.

questions.q: Add a prefix to 'kind' to make its opposite.
questions.e: The prefix un- makes kind into unkind.

questions.q: Which word rhymes with 'seas' in the first stanza: these, sky or rivers?
questions.e: Seas and these rhyme at the ends of lines 2 and 4.

questions.q: The poet says the rainbow 'overtops the ______'.
questions.e: Overtops the trees means the rainbow rises higher than the trees.

questions.q: By the time we reached the station, the train ______. (leave)
questions.e: The past perfect (had left) shows an action completed before another past action.

questions.q: Write the past participle (third form) of 'write'.
questions.e: Write, wrote, written.

questions.q: Write the comparative of 'many'.
questions.e: Many is irregular: many, more, most.

questions.q: Make an adverb from 'happy'.
questions.e: Change y to i and add ly: happily.

questions.q: Divide the sweets ______ the three children.
questions.e: Among is used for more than two; between is used for two.

questions.q: ______ it was raining, we went out to play.
questions.e: Although shows that something happened in spite of something else.

questions.q: Write a synonym of 'brave'.
questions.e: Courageous and bold mean the same as brave.

questions.q: 'What a lovely garden!' is an ______ sentence.
questions.e: A sentence showing strong feeling and ending with ! is exclamatory.

questions.q: Write the abstract noun of 'brave'.
questions.e: Bravery names the quality of being brave, so it is an abstract noun.

questions.q: This is the boy ______ won the race.
questions.e: Who is a relative pronoun used for people as the subject.

questions.q: Read: 'There are bridges on the rivers, as pretty as you please; but the bow that bridges heaven, and overtops the trees...'
p: (a) What is there on the rivers?
(b) Which word in these lines rhymes with 'please'?
(c) Which is prettier, the bridges or the rainbow?
questions.e: The poet compares man-made bridges with the rainbow and finds the rainbow prettier far than these.

questions.q: Change the tense of: Meera writes a story.
questions.e: Write becomes wrote (past), has written (present perfect) and will write (future).

questions.q: Name the kind of each sentence.
p: (b) The sun rises in the east.
questions.e: A question is interrogative, a statement is declarative (assertive), and a request or command is imperative.

questions.q: Answer the word questions.
questions.e: Victory is the opposite of defeat; quickly means rapidly; right and write sound alike.

questions.q: Read: The team of players won the match in Kolkata.
p: (c) Find the common noun that names people.
questions.e: Team is a collective noun, Kolkata is a proper noun and players is a common noun.

questions.q: Arjun runs the ______ of all in his class. (fast)
questions.e: When comparing more than two, use the superlative: fastest.

questions.q: Riya has been ill ______ Monday.
questions.e: Since is used with a point of time; for is used with a period of time.

questions.q: He worked hard ______ he could pass the exam.
questions.e: So that shows purpose.

questions.t: Hornbill: The Portrait of a Lady
questions.q: Who is the author of 'The Portrait of a Lady'?
questions.e: 'The Portrait of a Lady' is Khushwant Singh's affectionate sketch of his grandmother.

questions.t: Hornbill: The Portrait of a Lady
questions.q: In the village, while returning from the temple school, the grandmother threw stale chapattis to the village ______.
questions.e: She carried stale chapattis and threw them to the village dogs that followed them home.

questions.t: Hornbill: The Portrait of a Lady
questions.q: After they moved to the city, the grandmother spent her afternoons feeding the ______.
questions.e: In the city she found a new pastime: sitting in the courtyard feeding bread crumbs to the sparrows.

questions.t: Hornbill: The Portrait of a Lady
questions.q: The grandmother was upset when the author began to learn ______ at his English school, as she thought it was meant only for harlots and beggars.
questions.e: She disapproved of music lessons, believing music was not meant for gentlefolk.

questions.t: Hornbill: The Portrait of a Lady
questions.q: For how many years did the author stay abroad before his grandmother received him back at the railway station?
questions.e: The author went abroad for further studies and was away for five years.

questions.t: Hornbill: The Portrait of a Lady
questions.q: On the evening of the author's return, the grandmother did not pray. Answer about this evening and her death.
p: (a) Which instrument did she beat while singing with the women of the neighbourhood?
(b) Her songs were about the homecoming of whom?
(c) Which birds came in thousands and sat silently around her dead body?
questions.e: She celebrated his return by beating an old drum and singing of the homecoming of warriors; when she died, thousands of sparrows sat silently around her body.

questions.t: Hornbill: We're Not Afraid to Die
questions.q: What was the name of the boat on which the narrator's family sailed around the world?
questions.e: The family sailed in the Wavewalker, a 23-metre boat they had prepared for the voyage.

questions.t: Hornbill: We're Not Afraid to Die
questions.q: From which English port did the voyage begin in July 1976?
questions.e: The narrator, his wife Mary and their children set sail from Plymouth, England, in July 1976.

questions.t: Hornbill: We're Not Afraid to Die
questions.q: The family wanted to duplicate the round-the-world voyage made 200 years earlier by Captain James ______.
questions.e: Their dream was to repeat the famous round-the-world voyage of Captain James Cook.

questions.t: Hornbill: We're Not Afraid to Die
questions.q: On which tiny island in the Indian Ocean did the badly damaged boat finally reach safety?
questions.e: With careful navigation they reached Ile Amsterdam, a tiny French island in the southern Indian Ocean.

questions.t: Hornbill: We're Not Afraid to Die
questions.q: Two crewmen joined the family to help with the dangerous southern Indian Ocean crossing.
p: (a) What was the first name of the American crewman?
(b) What was the first name of the Swiss crewman?
(c) What was the name of the narrator's daughter, who was hurt in the storm?
questions.e: Larry Vigil (American) and Herb Seigler (Swiss) joined the crew; the narrator's daughter Sue was injured but showed great courage.

questions.q: Who discovered the tomb of Tutankhamun in 1922?
questions.e: British archaeologist Howard Carter discovered Tut's tomb in 1922.

questions.q: Tutankhamun's tomb lies in the Valley of the ______ in Egypt.
questions.e: Tut was buried in the Valley of the Kings near Luxor.

questions.q: Which machine was used in 2005 to study Tut's mummy and produce a detailed 3-D image of it?
questions.a: CT scanner|CT scan|CT|CT machine|computed tomography|computed tomography scanner
questions.e: A CT (computed tomography) scanner took hundreds of X-ray images that a computer combined into a 3-D picture.

questions.q: Akhenaten, believed to be Tut's father, promoted the worship of a single god, the sun disk, called the ______.
questions.e: Akhenaten promoted the Aten (sun disk); Tut later changed his name from Tutankhaten to Tutankhamun, restoring Amun.

questions.q: Who wrote 'The Ailing Planet: the Green Movement's Role'?
questions.e: The essay was written by the eminent jurist Nani Palkhivala.

questions.q: The notice 'You are looking at the most dangerous animal in the world' was found in a zoo at Lusaka, the capital of ______.
questions.e: The essay mentions this notice in a cage at the zoo in Lusaka, Zambia.
