questions.q: What does a visitor actually see inside that cage at the Lusaka zoo?
questions.e: The cage contains only a mirror, showing that man himself is the most dangerous animal.

questions.q: The idea of 'sustainable development' was popularised by the World Commission on Environment and Development, also called the ______ Commission.
questions.e: The Brundtland Commission (1987) defined sustainable development as meeting present needs without compromising the needs of future generations.

questions.q: The essay names the earth's four principal biological systems: fisheries, forests, grasslands and ______.
questions.e: Fisheries, forests, grasslands and croplands form the foundation of the global economic system and supply our food and raw materials.

questions.q: Who wrote the poem 'The Voice of the Rain'?
questions.e: 'The Voice of the Rain' is by the American poet Walt Whitman.

questions.q: Who is the poet of 'A Photograph'?
questions.e: 'A Photograph' was written by Shirley Toulson about an old photograph of her mother.

questions.q: In 'The Voice of the Rain', the rain describes itself as the ______ of Earth.
questions.e: The rain says, 'I am the Poem of Earth', comparing its cycle to that of a song or poem.

questions.q: In 'A Photograph', where were the poet's mother and her two cousins when the photograph was taken?
questions.e: The photograph shows the mother, about twelve, paddling at the beach with her two girl cousins.

questions.t: Snapshots: The Summer of the Beautiful White Horse
questions.q: Who is the author of 'The Summer of the Beautiful White Horse'?
questions.e: The story is by the Armenian-American writer William Saroyan.

questions.t: Snapshots: The Summer of the Beautiful White Horse
questions.q: What was the name of the narrator's cousin who had a way with horses?
questions.e: Cousin Mourad, thirteen, was considered crazy by everyone and had a way with horses.

questions.t: Snapshots: The Summer of the Beautiful White Horse
questions.q: How old was the narrator, Aram, when the story took place?
questions.e: Aram says he was nine years old when Mourad came to his house with the white horse.

questions.t: Snapshots: The Summer of the Beautiful White Horse
questions.q: The boys belonged to a tribe famous for its honesty. Name the tribe.
questions.e: The Garoghlanian tribe was known for honesty, which is why the boys could not be thought of as thieves.

questions.t: Snapshots: The Summer of the Beautiful White Horse
questions.q: Who was the real owner of the white horse?
questions.e: The horse belonged to John Byro, a farmer whose horse had been stolen a month earlier.

questions.t: Snapshots: The Summer of the Beautiful White Horse
questions.q: The boys hid the horse while its owner searched for it.
p: (a) What was the nationality of the farmer John Byro?
(b) In whose deserted vineyard barn did the boys hide the horse?
(c) 'It is no harm; pay no attention to it' was the favourite line of Uncle ______.
questions.e: John Byro was an Assyrian farmer; the boys hid the horse in the barn of Fetvajian's deserted vineyard; Uncle Khosrove always said 'It is no harm; pay no attention to it.'

questions.q: Who wrote the story 'The Address'?
questions.e: 'The Address' is by the Dutch writer Marga Minco and is set after the Second World War.

questions.q: What was the name of the woman who took away the mother's belongings for 'safe keeping'?
questions.e: Mrs Dorling, an old acquaintance, carried away the family's valuables during the war.

questions.q: Mrs Dorling lived at Marconi Street, number ______.
questions.e: The mother told her daughter the address: Number 46, Marconi Street.

questions.q: The narrator recognised her mother's piece of clothing on the woman who opened the door. What was it?
questions.a: cardigan|green cardigan|green knitted cardigan|a green knitted cardigan|knitted cardigan
questions.e: The woman wore a green knitted cardigan with pale wooden buttons, which had belonged to the narrator's mother.

questions.q: Who wrote the play 'Mother's Day'?
questions.e: 'Mother's Day' is a comic one-act play by J.B. Priestley.

questions.q: Mrs Pearson's neighbour, a strong woman who tells fortunes, is Mrs ______.
questions.e: Mrs Fitzgerald exchanges personalities with Mrs Pearson to teach her family a lesson.

questions.q: Mrs Pearson's family takes her for granted. Name the family members.
p: (a) What is the name of Mrs Pearson's daughter?
(b) What is the name of her son?
(c) What is the name of her husband?
questions.e: Doris, Cyril and George Pearson treat Mrs Pearson like a servant until Mrs Fitzgerald, in her body, puts them in their place.

questions.q: Who is the author of the story 'Birth'?
questions.e: 'Birth' is an extract from A.J. Cronin's novel 'The Citadel'.

questions.q: Name the young doctor who attended Susan Morgan's delivery.
questions.e: Dr Andrew Manson, newly qualified, attended the case and saved both mother and baby.

questions.q: To revive the stillborn baby, the doctor dipped it alternately into basins of hot and ______ water.
questions.e: Andrew plunged the baby alternately into hot and ice-cold water and rubbed it until it began to breathe.

questions.t: Snapshots: The Tale of Melon City
questions.q: Who wrote 'The Tale of Melon City'?
questions.e: 'The Tale of Melon City' is a humorous narrative poem by Vikram Seth.

questions.t: Snapshots: The Tale of Melon City
questions.q: The just and placid king ordered an ______ to be built across the thoroughfare.
questions.e: The king wanted an arch across the main road to edify the spectator.

questions.t: Snapshots: The Tale of Melon City
questions.q: The arch was built so low that, while riding under it, the king lost his ______.
questions.e: The low arch knocked off the king's crown, and he declared it a disgrace.

questions.t: Snapshots: The Tale of Melon City
questions.q: When the next man to pass the City Gate (an idiot) was asked who should be king, he named a fruit. Which one?
questions.e: The idiot said 'A melon', so the people crowned a melon, and the place came to be called Melon City.

questions.q: Fill in the blank with a suitable determiner: There is hardly ______ milk left in the jug.
questions.e: 'Hardly' is negative in meaning, so it is followed by 'any'; 'milk' is uncountable, ruling out 'many' and 'few'.

questions.q: Complete the passive form: 'Meera wrote a letter.' becomes 'A letter ______ by Meera.'
questions.e: Simple past active becomes 'was/were + past participle' in the passive: 'A letter was written by Meera.'

questions.q: Fill in each blank with the correct form of the verb given in brackets.
p: (a) The train ______ (leave) before we reached the station.
(b) By next March, Arjun ______ (complete) his course.
questions.e: Past perfect shows the earlier of two past actions; future perfect shows an action finished before a future time; present continuous shows an action happening now.

questions.q: Write the antonym of 'ancient'.
questions.e: 'Ancient' means very old; its opposite is 'modern'.

questions.q: One word for 'a person who does not believe in the existence of God' is ______.
questions.e: An atheist denies God's existence; an agnostic is unsure, and a theist believes in God.

questions.q: Give one word for each of the following.
p: (a) A place where bees are kept
(b) A speech made without any preparation
questions.e: An apiary is a place for keeping bees; an extempore (impromptu) speech is unprepared; hydrophobia is fear of water.

questions.q: Who is the author of 'The Last Lesson'?
questions.e: 'The Last Lesson' was written by the French writer Alphonse Daudet.

questions.q: What was the name of the French teacher who gave the last lesson?
questions.e: M. Hamel had taught French in the village school for forty years.

questions.q: The order had come from ______ that only German would be taught in the schools of Alsace and Lorraine.
questions.e: After the Prussian victory, the order from Berlin banned the teaching of French in Alsace and Lorraine.

questions.q: Franz was afraid of being scolded because he had not learnt the rules for ______.
questions.e: M. Hamel had said he would question the class on participles, and Franz did not know the first word about them.

questions.q: What did M. Hamel write on the blackboard at the end of the last lesson?
questions.e: Too moved to speak, M. Hamel wrote 'Vive La France!' (Long live France) in large letters.

questions.q: Who wrote 'Lost Spring: Stories of Stolen Childhood'?
questions.e: 'Lost Spring' is an excerpt from Anees Jung's book of the same name.

questions.q: Saheb's family left ______ in 1971 after storms swept away their fields and homes, and settled in Seemapuri.
questions.e: Saheb's family came from Dhaka (Bangladesh) in 1971 and settled among ragpickers in Seemapuri.

questions.q: Mukesh's family at Firozabad is engaged in which traditional work?
questions.e: Firozabad is the centre of India's glass-blowing and bangle-making industry.

questions.q: Unlike others in his family, Mukesh dreams of becoming a motor ______.
questions.e: Mukesh insists on being his own master and wants to be a motor mechanic, learning to drive a car.

questions.q: Saheb is a young ragpicker in Seemapuri.
p: lord of the universe|lord of universe
(c) Where does Saheb later start working?
tea stall|a tea stall|tea-stall|at a tea stall
questions.e: Saheb-e-Alam means 'lord of the universe', an irony; he later works at a tea stall for 800 rupees a month and loses his carefree freedom.

questions.q: Who is the author of 'Deep Water'?
questions.a: William O. Douglas|William Douglas|Douglas|William O Douglas
questions.e: 'Deep Water' is from 'Of Men and Mountains' by William O. Douglas.

questions.q: Douglas decided to learn swimming at the ______ pool, which was safe because it was shallow at one end.
questions.e: He chose the Y.M.C.A. pool, which was only two or three feet deep at the shallow end.

questions.q: Which river, warned against by his mother as treacherous, made Douglas choose the pool instead?
questions.e: The Yakima River was considered treacherous and had drowned many, so his mother warned him against it.

questions.q: To finally test that his terror had gone, Douglas swam two miles across Lake ______ in New Hampshire.
questions.e: He swam across Lake Wentworth and later Warm Lake, finding that the residual terror had fled.

questions.q: Douglas quotes President Roosevelt at the end: 'All we have to fear is ______ itself.'
questions.e: Having conquered his fear of water, Douglas understood Roosevelt's words that the real enemy is fear itself.

questions.q: Who wrote 'The Rattrap'?
questions.e: 'The Rattrap' is by the Swedish writer Selma Lagerlöf, the first woman to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.

questions.q: How many kronor did the old crofter proudly show the peddler?
questions.e: The crofter showed three ten-kronor notes, thirty kronor, which the peddler later stole.

questions.q: What was the name of the ironmaster's daughter who treated the peddler kindly?
questions.e: Edla Willmansson persuaded the peddler to stay for Christmas even after the truth came out.

questions.q: The ironmaster mistook the peddler for his old regimental comrade, Captain von ______.
questions.e: The ironmaster believed the peddler was Captain von Ståhle, an old army friend down on his luck.

questions.q: The peddler spent Christmas at the ironmaster's house and left a gift before going.
p: (a) Name the ironworks owned by the ironmaster.
(b) What did the peddler leave as a Christmas present for Edla?
(c) What was found inside the present, to be returned to the crofter?
money|kronor|thirty kronor|30 kronor|ten-kronor notes|three ten-kronor notes
questions.e: At Ramsjö he left Edla a small rattrap containing the crofter's stolen thirty kronor, showing his redemption through her kindness.

questions.q: Who wrote 'Indigo'?
questions.e: 'Indigo' is an extract from Louis Fischer's 'The Life of Mahatma Gandhi'.

questions.q: Which poor sharecropper persuaded Gandhi to visit Champaran?
questions.e: Rajkumar Shukla, an illiterate but resolute sharecropper, followed Gandhi everywhere until he agreed to come.

questions.q: Gandhi met Rajkumar Shukla at the annual convention of the Indian National Congress held at ______ in December 1916.
questions.e: Shukla approached Gandhi at the Lucknow Congress session of December 1916.

questions.q: Under the long-term contract, the sharecroppers had to plant what percentage of their land with indigo?
questions.e: They had to plant three-twentieths, or 15 per cent, of their holdings with indigo and give it as rent.

questions.q: Gandhi's work in Bihar led to a settlement with the British planters.
p: (a) In which district of Bihar did the indigo struggle take place?
(b) Which English pacifist did Gandhi's lawyer friends want to keep with them, though Gandhi refused?
C.F. Andrews|CF Andrews|C F Andrews|Andrews|Charles Freer Andrews
(c) What percentage of the money did the planters finally agree to refund?
questions.e: In Champaran, Gandhi refused C.F. Andrews' help to make the peasants self-reliant, and accepted a 25 per cent refund to break the planters' prestige.

questions.q: Who wrote 'Poets and Pancakes'?
questions.e: 'Poets and Pancakes' is an excerpt from Asokamitran's 'My Years with Boss', about Gemini Studios.

questions.q: 'Pancake' was the brand name of the ______ material bought in truckloads by Gemini Studios.
questions.e: Pancake was the make-up brand used to make actors look presentable under the bright lights.

questions.q: Which English poet visited Gemini Studios, though nobody there understood what he said?
questions.e: Stephen Spender, editor of 'The Encounter', addressed the studio staff, who could not follow his accent or poetry.

questions.q: Who wrote 'My Mother at Sixty-six'?
questions.e: 'My Mother at Sixty-six' is by Kamala Das.

questions.q: In 'Keeping Quiet', the poet asks us to count up to which number and keep still?
questions.e: Neruda says, 'Now we will count to twelve and we will all keep still.'

questions.q: 'A Thing of Beauty' is an extract from John Keats's long poem ______.
questions.e: The lines 'A thing of beauty is a joy for ever' open Keats's 'Endymion'.

questions.q: In 'Aunt Jennifer's Tigers', the tigers are called 'Bright topaz ______ of a world of green'.
questions.e: 'Denizens' means inhabitants; the tigers belong to the green jungle world Aunt Jennifer creates.

questions.q: In 'My Mother at Sixty-six', the poet was driving from her parents' home to which airport?
questions.e: The poet was driving to Cochin airport when she noticed how pale and aged her mother looked.

questions.q: Who is the author of 'The Third Level'?
questions.e: 'The Third Level' is a short story by Jack Finney.

questions.q: At which railway station in New York did Charley find the third level?
questions.a: Grand Central Station|Grand Central|Grand Central Terminal
questions.e: Charley lost his way in Grand Central Station and stumbled onto a third level that officially did not exist.

questions.q: To which town in Illinois did Charley want to buy two tickets?
questions.e: Charley wanted to take his wife to Galesburg, a peaceful town of the 1890s.

questions.q: Charley's experience at the third level affects the people around him.
p: (a) What is the name of Charley's wife?
(b) What is the first name of his psychiatrist friend?
(c) In which year was the newspaper Charley saw on the third level printed?
questions.e: Louisa is Charley's wife; Sam Weiner, his psychiatrist friend, later disappears and is found in Galesburg; the newspaper on the third level was dated 1894.

questions.q: Who wrote 'The Tiger King'?
questions.e: 'The Tiger King' is a satire by Kalki (R. Krishnamurthy).

questions.q: The Tiger King was the Maharaja of ______.
questions.e: The Tiger King was Jung Jung Bahadur, Maharaja of Pratibandapuram.

questions.q: How many tigers did the Maharaja vow to kill after the astrologers' prediction?
questions.e: The astrologers said a tiger would cause his death, so he vowed to kill a hundred tigers.

questions.q: The Maharaja died from an infection caused by a sliver from a wooden toy ______.
questions.e: A sliver of the crudely carved wooden tiger pierced his hand, and the infection killed him — the hundredth tiger took its revenge.

questions.t: Vistas: Journey to the End of the Earth
questions.q: Who wrote 'Journey to the End of the Earth'?
questions.e: Tishani Doshi describes her journey to Antarctica in this chapter.

questions.t: Vistas: Journey to the End of the Earth
questions.q: About 650 million years ago, India and Antarctica were part of the supercontinent ______.
questions.e: Gondwana was a giant southern supercontinent that included present-day India and Antarctica.

questions.t: Vistas: Journey to the End of the Earth
questions.q: The 'Students on Ice' programme, which took the author to Antarctica, was headed by the Canadian Geoff ______.
questions.e: Geoff Green founded 'Students on Ice' to take high school students to the polar regions.

questions.q: Who wrote 'The Enemy'?
questions.a: Pearl S. Buck|Pearl Buck|Pearl S Buck|Buck
questions.e: 'The Enemy' is a story by the American writer Pearl S. Buck.

questions.q: What was the name of Dr Sadao's wife?
questions.e: Hana, Sadao's wife, helped him nurse the wounded enemy soldier.

questions.q: The wounded prisoner of war washed up on the shore near Sadao's house was from which country?
questions.e: The man was an escaped American prisoner of war, which made sheltering him a crime in wartime Japan.

questions.q: Write the antonym of 'reluctant'.
questions.e: 'Reluctant' means unwilling; its opposite is 'willing' or 'eager'.

questions.q: Give one word for each of the following.
p: (b) A person who speaks many languages
questions.e: Democracy is rule by the people; a polyglot knows many languages; illegible means impossible to read.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks to change each sentence into indirect speech.
p: (a) He said, "I am tired." → He said that he ______ tired.
(b) She said to me, "Where do you live?" → She asked me where I ______.
(c) The teacher said, "The earth moves round the sun." → The teacher said that the earth ______ round the sun.
questions.e: With a past reporting verb, present tense changes to past ('am' to 'was', 'live' to 'lived'), but universal truths keep the present tense.
